utterances.text: That's correct, and that would be the 18th and the 24th of August, if that's correct.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again this interview took place in Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both of them did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could we move, Your Honour, just for a second in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention, Mr. Bouckaert, to page 10 of your statement -- of your report, I'm sorry. And that's again P352. And I would simply draw your attention to the third indented paragraph on that page, and that's the quote which you attribute, I understand, to Mr. Aziz Bajrami. Perhaps we'll go simply to the previous page to establish that matter. I apologise. Mr. Bouckaert, if you look at the bottom of page 9, is that correct that there is -- the very last paragraph, there's an indented paragraph which is your record of what Mr. Aziz Bajrami told you at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, to page 10, please. And I'd like to read out to you the last paragraph which you record from Mr. Bajrami. It says: "I thought that something would happen, so I quickly went back to the garden door and went out. Then I heard shooting. That is when they killed Muharem with two or three shots." The question, Mr. Bouckaert, is: Did Mr. Bajrami tell you that he had witnessed the killing himself or that he had been told that he had witnessed -- sorry, that he had been told that Muharem had been killed in this manner; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that he witnessed the killing himself. He was trying to flee from the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. There's another matter that I would like to ask you questions about and that's the -- your findings about the alleged presence of the NLA in the village at that time. Do you recall this part of your report?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you expressed the view in your report that you had -- and in the letters which you subsequently wrote or the interviews which you subsequently gave, that you had not found any evidence of the presence of the NLA in the village at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had found no evidence of the presence of the NLA in the area that we looked at, that's correct, although I would like to just mention that our report -- our report's legal conclusions state that even if the NLA rebels responsible for the antitank mine incident were present in Ljuboten, the attack on Ljuboten by the Macedonian police, as documented by Human Rights Watch, involved both indiscriminate and deliberate attacks on civilians in violation of the norms of IHL and international human rights law.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Is that correct also that none of the villagers that you interviewed mentioned the presence of the NLA in the village on that day?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they only mentioned the presence of an NLA position above the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you did not query this matter with any of the Macedonian authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Macedonian authorities had made general statements that the people who had been killed were terrorists, but they had presented no specific evidence to show that there had been an NLA presence in public at the time of the issuing of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm simply asking you, Mr. Bouckaert: Did you ask the army or the Ministry of Defence whether they had any information in that regard?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you ask the police or the Ministry of Interior if they had information in that regard?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you ask the Ministry of Justice if they had any information in that regard?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you ask the Court or the Investigative Judge or the Prosecutor whether they had information in that regard?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you ask the security services whether they had information in that regard?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only person I briefed on our findings within the government at that time was the national security adviser.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would be Mr. Panderevski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you ask the OSCE whether they had any such information?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had discussions with the OSCE and also with the ICRC around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you seek formally to obtain information about this matter from either of those organisations?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not formally.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you seek information in that regard from the EUMM, the European Monitors?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No, we didn't -- I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also that you had been aware that in June of 2001, a number of journalists had met with members of the NLA in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: With uniformed members of the NLA, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is a point of methodology which I would like to go back. Do you remember that I asked you about your methodology in relation to, I think the report called "Fatal Strike," that's your southern Lebanon report; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you explained that in this particular report you sought to establish, from sources outside of Hezbollah influence, whether there had or hadn't been any presence of Hezbollah at the time of the targeting; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also said that where you couldn't find such outside information, you would drop the particular incident from your finding in the report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also that in the Ljuboten investigation, you put the onus on the government rather than on yourself and by that I mean that you asked and expected the Macedonian authority to actively provide you with information pertaining to this matter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I draw your attention again to your report once again, and it's P352 at page 16, 1-6, in particular to the third paragraph of that document where you said this -- I'll wait perhaps until you have it in front of you.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says: "It is significant that the government has not presented any credible evidence that there was an NLA presence in Ljuboten, such as confiscated NLA weapons or uniform, despite the growing international concern about the events in the village. Ordinarily, the government displays captured weapons and uniform in the aftermath of successful operations against the NLA." Is that correct that the situation is as follows: You indicated in your report that you had found no evidence of NLA presence, but that you had sought no information from sources outside of the village of Ljuboten to confirm or affirm this finding?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you say what request or application you made to obtain that information outside of the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well,, what is not correct in your question is that we sought no information from sources outside of the village of Ljuboten to confirm or affirm this finding. As I explained to you, I did have conversations with the OSCE, with the ICRC, and with a large number of journalists, and I found no evidence to indicate -- no information to indicate that our findings on the NLA presence were incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D24. And that's again the special report of the OSCE on the Ljuboten incidents which I showed to you earlier. And if I can ask the Registry perhaps to move to the second page of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, if you could look at the first paragraph at the top of the page, I'll read it out to you. It's the first full sentence, it starts: "A government mortar position is now clearly visible on one hilltop above the fields from the position of one of the bodies. In addition to the mortar emplacement outside the town, as noted herein, there is an ethnic Albanian armed group, EAAG presence in town as well." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can go now to the very bottom --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is referring to a presence after the attack on Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bouckaert, this is the report about the 12th of August --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which was made on the 16th, and it's referring to the burning of Macedonian homes in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bouckaert, perhaps we can go back --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition -- let me read the sentence for the record: "In addition to the mortar emplacement outside the town, as noted herein, there is an ethnic Albanian armed presence in town as well. Within a day of the team's visit to the mission, the mission received the reports that Macedonian houses in the village had been fired upon and burnt." So the EAAG presence refers to a presence on the 14th or 15th. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if perhaps we look at the last paragraph on that page, we may get some clarity on that point. It says this: "Second, OSCE monitors sound rather clear about the sequence of events at the village and, not surprisingly, their reports differ dramatically from press reports and commonly repeated tales. It is now known that there is an EAAG position north of the village, a significant position located in the area of Ljubotenski Racila," and that should be "Bacila". "Reliable sources indicate that the second position may have been associated with the mine strike on government forces in the area and that Macedonian forces appropriately engaged this EAAG positions with mortar fire below the village." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's talking about a position that is mentioned in our report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say this: "On 12 August at 805 hours, the first mortar round fell on the village. It landed in the vicinity of the Orthodox Church in the Macedonian section of the village. Two more rounds followed, each closer to the church. All three are believed to have been 120-millimetre mortars. These are more likely to have been EAAG rounds than government's and were the first shots fired into the village. Thereafter, the army fired on the Albanian side of the village with its similar-calibre mortars." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say this. It's the last sentence of the next paragraph, Mr. Bouckaert: "Reports from other international observers in the area indicate that there were EAAG in the village in civilian clothes and that there was an exchange of fire from deer rifle within the village." Are you still of the view that this report refers to a time after the events, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but there was quite fierce discussions within the OSCE at the time between Mr. Bolton and the human dimensions officer about the reliability of the latter information, about the reports from other international observers, which I believe refers to reports from the European Union monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can show you this document, Mr. Bouckaert. It's Exhibit 1D126 -- sorry, it's now Exhibit 1D29.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just would like to state that we did not consider some of these alternative theories advanced by the OSCE to be based on reliable information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. If you can perhaps look at the top left-hand corner of the document, Mr. Bouckaert. This is a document which comes from the EUMM. We understand it's Monitor Skopje to HQ EUMM, and it's dated the 13th of August of 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if you can look at the last part of this document, under the subheading "Security," it says the following: "Reports of fierce exchanges between ARM," and that's the Macedonian army, "and EEAG in the Ljuboten and Ljubanci area at 1400 hours," and then it says "12 August" it should be -- It says 12 July --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "12 July" and should be "12 August."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. Thank you. "Were confirmed late in the day by ICRC who had attempted to organise a convoy of vehicles to extract Albanian citizens of Ljuboten from the affected area." And then it says, "The ICRC attempted to conduct the extraction of an estimated 1.000 people along the secondary road running south from Ljuboten-Butel. The primary road south from Ljuboten runs through the Macedonian town of Radisani and it was known that there was a hostile gathering of townspeople awaiting the arrival of the displaced Albanians." Then it says: "The ICRC team reported that when they arrived at the spot between a police checkpoint and an army checkpoint in the general area, DM 385580, they encountered a roadblock manned by armed civilians who were abusive and chased them away from the area." And then it just concludes by saying: "The ICRC team was forced to abandon the attempt to rescue the displaced." Is that correct, that again according to the ICRC there had been what they say are fierce exchanges between the army and the EEAG in Ljuboten on 12th August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there was a mistaken conclusion by the ICRC which was not repeated later on. At that time, they did not gain access to the village. As the statement says, they came up to the village and had to leave because of the hostile presence of an ethnic Macedonian crowd. They heard fierce gunfire coming from Ljuboten, and they made a mistaken assumption, as many people would make, that it was an exchange of gunfire between the NLA and the Macedonian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D28, please. This is a report obtained by the Defence through an embassy here in The Hague, and as you can see, it's an EUMM situation report on fire on 12th August at 1600 hours, and the description of the general situation is this: "Macedonian security forces continued massive attacks against positions of rebel National Liberation Army positions in the Tetovo area and northeast along the road to the Kosovo border. NLA has moved closer to Skopje by gaining control over the village of Ljuboten, five kilometres north of Skopje outskirts." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this is based on information from the Crisis Management Centre which turned out to be absolutely incorrect, as was the information provided by the Crisis Management Centre the same day that 300 NLA members had crossed into Macedonia from Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on what evidence are you able to base your evidence to the effect that the information that I read to you was incorrect?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was not repeated by these agencies later on. This is reporting information directly received from the Crisis Management Centre, and during my meetings with the OSCE and the ICRC later on, these kind of reports were seen as inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. Bouckaert, that the Crisis Management Centre received information from the field from both the police and the army at times?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if I can --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a coordination body that managed the information during the crisis and then passed on the information to the various monitoring missions on the ground in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the witness can please be shown what is now Exhibit 1D26, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As you can see, this is a report in relation to military activities on the 12th of August of 2001, and it is signed by Lieutenant Brasnjarski, Darko, and it is a document that has been provided to us by the Prosecution. Mr. Brasnarski records the following. He says: "On the 12th August 2001, while conducting my regular duties in organising the work during the day, we were informed about 8.00 that machine-gun and sniper fire was opened against the position Smok from Ljuboten village." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then he says that: "We went immediately together with Lieutenant Jurisic, Jurisic Mario, towards the position." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if you go down a further, he says that: "The mortar actions started the action against targets in Ljuboten village as a support of our position. At about 9.20, a sniper fire was opened against the position at B-1 and during this a helmet that was on sandbags was hit and damaged. Immediately after that, also, machine-gun fire was opened against us from the houses left from the mosques." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then he says, a sentence later: "I fired six projectiles towards the house where the machine-gun fire was coming, and that was neutralised, whereas from the house under the mosque, the sniper continued to shoot, so I fired five projectiles against it and it was destroyed." You would agree, I hope, Mr. Bouckaert, that this suggests that at least there was fire coming from the village towards the position of the army on the 12th of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what this statement says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if Mr. Bouckaert could be shown what is 1D25, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, this is a similar report, a report of a similar nature. It's again from the Army of Macedonia and was again provided to us by the Office of the Prosecution. It's a report related to military activities on 12th August 2001, and it's signed by the commander of a mortar battery, 120-millimetres, Mr. Captain Grozdanovski, Nikolce, and the report says the following: "On 12 August 2001 in the morning, I was at the rest house performing my regular duties. At about eight hour we heard many long-lasting, repeated shots. Later, the commander of the battalion called me and ordered me to visit the observation post at the check-point Smok and to prepare the battery for action." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can go one sentence further down, it starts with the words: "From the observation towards the village, I realised that the terrorists were firing from the area of the church, from an old house about 100 metres on to the mosque. Most probably there was a sniper, whereas above the mosque, from the new houses, the second one, there was a machine-gun firing towards us. Then I informed the commander about the situation and he ordered me to destroy those positions with several mortar shells from 120-millimetre mortars." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again you would agree that this document would suggest that there was fire from the village towards the position of the army outside of the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what this document claims.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you indicated as well that you didn't have any information from -- or that you didn't seek to obtain any information from the Ministry of Interior or the police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is now Exhibit 1D20.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, this is the daily bulletin which is shared at the CMC, and it comes from the archives of the OSCE in Skopje. And if the Registry could go to page 12 of that document, please. Sorry, Mr. Bouckaert, perhaps I should just read out to you the period on the cover page that you might not --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can still see it in the Macedonian one. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So it covers the period from 18 hours on the 9th of August to 18 hours on the 10th of August. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can turn to page 12, please. It would be 1D00-1618. Thank you. And if you can focus your attention on the last annotation in this page, Mr. Bouckaert, number 37. It says the following: "16," and that's the time, "At 1530 hours a patrol from the police station Mirkovci reported that in the house of the family Zendolovski [phoen] In the village of Ljuboten, three persons were registered in black uniforms and armed with automatic weapons." My question, Mr. Bouckaert, is: Were you aware of such reports of armed men in black uniforms in the village on the 9th or 10th of August, in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown once again what has now been admitted, I believe, as Exhibit 1D87.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, this again the same document. I have shown you the second page of that document twice. I would like now you to focus on the last paragraph on the first page with the assistance of the Registry. This is again the record of an interview with an operative source by the UBK, and the source said this: "According to Odza, shots could be heard continually on the night between 8th and 9th August 2001, all coming from the gardens of Duraki Kazim and Fazliu Nedzmedin, and responses to those shots came from the Basinec area. In any case, Dzavid held his last meeting with Ljuboten residents on the month of 9 August 2001, in the house of Osmani Saban. The following day, around 0900 hours, the terrorist attack occurred on Balinec killing eight ARM soldiers and wounding another eight. In that context, according to the source, that same night, after the fighting around Balinec, a large number of unknown individuals in black uniforms were seen in the gardens of the house of Duraki Kazim, Duraku Safit, and Fazliu Nedzmedin, as well as two vehicles, one belonging to OSCE and the other to the UNHDR. At the same time, it was noticed that the women, children, and elderly were leaving the village throughout the night around the river and through the fields in the direction of the village of Radisani." At the time of preparing your report, sir, did you have information of that sort of the presence of NLA members in the village of Ljuboten on the 8th or 9th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I also don't know of any reports from the ICRC or the UNHCR mentioning any meetings with large groups of men in black in Ljuboten on August 8th or 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's also the evidence of a particular witness which I would like you to consider. Your Honour, this is the evidence of Witness M-37, a Prosecution witness, of the 15th of May of 2007. It was an open session. It is at page 827 and 828 of the transcript. The witness was asked the following: "You said that occasionally you used binoculars to view the village; right?" The answer is: "Yes." And then the question: "There was sporadic gunfire from the village towards the check-points where you were; is that right?" And the answer is: "Whether there was gunfire from the direction of the village?" And he says: "Yes, and I think that was with -- that was a sniper rifle, and you were able to find one of those bullets in one of the house, it penetrated the walls of one of the houses in the village." So we'd agree that at least this particular witness gave the evidence -- gave evidence to the effect that there was, again, fire coming from the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yes, that's -- if that's what you read into the record, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've also indicated in your report that you did not find any evidence of defensive position. You said that of sandbagging and that sort of defensive position. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I had quite a more extensive list of things we were looking for, but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And none of the villagers indicated to you at any stage that any such positions had been prepared or made in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another document, which is identified as an Exhibit 1D30. Can you agree, Mr. Bouckaert, that any such defensive position could have been removed between the time that elapsed between the incident in the village of Ljuboten and the time when you visited the village; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is theoretically possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if you look at the documents which is now in front of you, this is a letter from the Prosecution. It's a record of an interview carried out by the Prosecution with a person whom the Prosecution intends to call as a witness, and this is the information which this person gave to the Prosecution: "During his duty as an intelligence officer, Kostadinov had personal contact with the person known as Kenan. He described this person as one of the village leaders of Ljuboten. Kenan took over the main authority to lead the village from the other village leader, the school teacher. Kostadinov describes the teacher as the person with the money and Kenan as the person with'power.' After the transfer of power to Kenan took place, the problems with the villagers in Ljuboten started. Kostadinov is sure, although he does not have evidence, that Kenan has NLA connections." He states that: "The ARM doesn't have a file about Kenan, but he recommends the DBK and the police station in Cair." And then he says: "With respect to the use of the term 'check-point' in his report to describe the resistance to approaching Macedonians faced on Sunday morning, 12th August, Kostadinov elaborated, it was a machine-gun outside in front of Kenan's house described as a weapon supporting ammunition by a belt, calibre 12 millimetre. The machine-gun was operated by three persons. The machine-gun was positioned by the cover of the terrain, and according to Kostadinov, no fortification like sandbags was used. The machine-gun was operated at the moment of the event. The witness is sure that the fortification or classical machine-gun post would definitely have been spotted by the observation points of the ARM. It is not clear if Kenan was present at the time." Do you agree, sir, that if the information provided by Mr. Kostadinov is to be believed, it would appear, in fact, to have been a defensive position of quite -- of some significance in the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person, Kenan, I actually spoke to. He was the head of the Civil Defence in Ljuboten, and he denied that there had been any such position in the village and spoke about an agreement that they had reached with the villages of Rastak and Ljubanci to keep the NLA out of the village. But I do agree that if this witness is accurate, that it would suggest that there was an NLA position or a machine-gun in the village. But that is contra -- actually, I should say it would suggest that there was a machine-gun in the village. But that was contrary to what Mr. Aliu told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct, that you did not take any step to verify -- I think I have made the point already, but you did not verify with the army whether they had spotted such a check-point or not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and no public information available at the time from the Macedonian authorities suggested that, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, when you say that, you indicate that you didn't make a request for any such information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's a few general questions which I would like to ask you about your experience of the NLA in general. There is a proposition which was made by Mr. Fred Abrahams in an interview which he gave, and I will place it in front of you so you can consult it. It's Rule 65 ter 1D406, and it's 1D00-3678. It's an interview given by Frederick Abrahams to "The Washington Post," and the date is the 27th of June, 2001. And if I could ask the Registry to move immediately to page 1D00-3685 of that document. Perhaps I should ask you this, Mr. Bouckaert, first: Is that correct that your organisation, as you indicated, I think, recorded quite a number of criminal incidents or crimes committed by members of the NLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without doubt, some were so serious that we felt that amnesty, which was part of the final peace agreement, should exclude them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will come back to the issue of amnesty in a moment, Mr. Bouckaert. The statement which I would like to read to you is the following. Mr. Abrahams is recorded as saying: "The NLA is an extreme and violent reflection of frustration felt by many ethnic Albanians. Although many Albanians don't agree with the means, they sympathise with the stated aims." Is that a statement with which you would agree, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. It should be page 1D --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the answer is just down the same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the page -- yes, thank you very much. It's the first paragraph with the bolded "Frederick Abrahams."

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I would agree with the assessment made by Mr. Abrahams if it was read in full, rather than just the first two lines of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I wanted to ask you first this part and then the second part, but would you agree with this first part or do you take issue with any of that statement, the first part of the statement of Mr. Abrahams?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not have used those same words.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you would agree that the NLA is, in fact, very -- I mean, it was regarded at the time as an extremist group and by many as a terrorist organisation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask you to slow down and make pauses.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was seen by many organisations this way. I would certainly not classify the NLA as a terrorist organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is that correct that a very large number of states regarded the NLA as a terrorist organisation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of a very large number of states, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, for instance, that it was the position of the OSCE General Assembly, for instance, or parliamentary assembly --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Parliamentary assembly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was a statement that was adopted by the parliamentarians at an OSCE meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it was also the position, for instance, of the United States; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think here we need to understand the context in which these diplomats were operating. The United States and many other states did not want to see a spread of violence and a destabilisation of Macedonia. They wanted to send a very clear message to the NLA that what had happened in Kosovo, in terms of an international armed intervention, would not be repeated, and they wanted to put the maximum amount of pressure on the NLA to put down their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is that correct that the NLA was regarded by the United States -- by the government of the United States as a terrorist organisation and called as such; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any statements from the United States describing the NLA as a terrorist organisation, and the NLA was not listed by the United States on its lists of terrorist organisations, which does list groups like Hamas and other groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we'll come back to that, then, later today or tomorrow. But is that correct also that the NLA was claiming, at all stages of the crisis, that they were abiding by the Geneva Conventions and other humanitarian law treaties?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although we've documented many violations of that commitment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that a common excuse for the leaders of the NLA, both -- or I should say the NLA or the KLA in Kosovo was to say that the crimes had been committed by splinter groups and not by the NLA or the KLA itself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I actually had such a conversation with Commander Matusi [phoen], who was one of the -- was the commander for the Tetovo area, when I discussed the case of the -- the road workers and the disappearances of ethnic Macedonians around Tetovo, he did try to claim that it was done by splinter groups rather than NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Your Honour, I don't think there's any need to tender the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, I would like to go back to one other finding in your report, and if I may ask you to go back to P352, that's your report, and turn to page 3 of that report.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of my report?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please. And if you can go under the "Recommendation," the first recommendation to the Macedonian authority. Is that correct that one of the recommendations you made was as follows, and I will read your words: "The authorities who carry out the investigation should be independent from the government agencies involved in the Ljuboten operation, particularly the Ministry of Interior." Is that correct that you made such a call? You called for an independent and transparent investigation by the Macedonian authorities which would exclude the Ministry of Interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it's a general principle that people should not investigate themselves for crimes, so, yes, that was part of our recommendation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct, that another recommendation which you made at the time was that Mr. Boskoski himself should be investigated for what you considered to be his acts and conduct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Conduct a credible, impartial and transparent investigation into the allegations of government abuses in Ljuboten, including the role of Minister of Interior Ljube Boskoski and the forces under his command.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you made a specific call for the investigation of Mr. Boskoski's own role in another context? Did you make a specific call for, and in particular to the Chief Prosecutor of this Tribunal, that the role of Mr. Boskoski should be investigated; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. There is -- I'm not sure I understand your question. Can you --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I'll show you the documents in question.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's Rule 65 ter 1D344, and it has an ERN 1D00-3263. There is only an English version. Mr. Bouckaert, this is a letter addressed to the Chief Prosecutor of this Tribunal, Carla Del Ponte. It's dated the 5th of September of 2001, and it concerns the Ljuboten investigation. If I may ask the Registry to turn to the third page of that document. I would like to ask you to focus your attention on the second paragraph of that document, which starts with the words: "We are troubled ..." Can you see that? Can you see it, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It reads as follows: "We are troubled by reports that Minister of Interior Ljube Boskoski was in Ljuboten on 12 August, the day that the worst abuses were committed. We respectfully request that your government commence a prompt investigation into his role and the conduct of Macedonian troops under his command. We note that in the absence of an appropriate response by your government, the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia is authorised to act, and we are forwarding our findings to the Tribunal." And it is signed by Ms. Elizabeth Andersen. It is sent to the President of Macedonia, Boris Trajkovski, c.c.'ed to the Prime Minister -- sorry, c.c.'ed to the embassy of Macedonia in Washington, to Mr. Goce Georgievski, and it's also c.c.'ed to Ms. Del Ponte, Prosecutor of the ICTY. Do you recall that letter?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, it's our position that the Macedonian authorities had a responsibility to investigate these serious abuses, and in the absence of efforts to investigate and punish those abuses, that this honourable Tribunal had jurisdiction over those crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also requested more specifically that the role of Mr. Boskoski be investigated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can go back to your report at page 3 again, this is P352. And again I'll ask you to look at the section called "The Recommendations." If the Registry could assist with the last paragraph but one. It starts with the word: "Cooperate ..." Thank you. Another recommendation which you made at the time of your report was: "Cooperate with international organisations, including the OSCE and the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, ICTY, in the efforts to monitor and investigate alleged violations of international human rights and humanitarian law by both sides to the conflict in Macedonia." Do you recall making that recommendation?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Going back to your first requests or recommendations to the Macedonian authority, did you make any inquiries at the time with the Ministry of Interior whether any investigation was ongoing at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you make any such inquiry with the Court in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: But actually the government's spokesperson had already made a statement at the time that investigations of -- the Macedonian investigations had concluded that no crimes had been committed in Ljuboten, and I believe that this is quoted in our report at some stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll try to take it one step at a time, Mr. Bouckaert. Did you make any inquiry with the Court in Macedonia whether there was any investigation into this matter?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you make any inquiry with an investigative judge or with a prosecutor to query whether there was an investigation at the time in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you make any such inquiry in the months following the events at Ljuboten with the Court, with the Prosecutor, or with the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our report was released on September 6th, five days before the tragic events of September 11th, and soon thereafter I went to Pakistan and Afghanistan to monitor the conflict there. So I personally did not play any further role in -- following the events of Ljuboten or the response of the government of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So just to clarify the matter, you personally did not make any such inquiry in the month following the report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know if your organisation, your colleagues, made any such inquiry with any of the Macedonian authorities at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D408. It has an ERN range 1D00-3689 to 3690.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, this is --

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall this letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if time permits, we will come back to the issue of amnesty, but for the time being would you confirm that this is a letter of Human Rights Watch? It's dated the 2nd October of 2001, and it's directed to the President of the Republic of Macedonia, Mr. Trajkovski.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did review this letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn, please, to -- well, I'll start reading perhaps from the bottom of this page, if I may ask, with the assistance of the Registry. Mr. Bouckaert, I'll start reading from the last two lines of that document. It says this: "We also take this opportunity, Mr. President, to call on the Macedonian authorities to objectively investigate the serious abuses against ethnic Albanian civilians committed by the government forces, which Human Rights Watch and other impartial monitors have brought to the government's attention." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then you say: "We are particularly concerned by the failure of the authorities to initiate an effective and credible investigation of the August 2001 events in the village of Ljuboten, as well as by reports that ethnic Macedonians paramilitary groups continue to intimidate and assault civilians." So is that correct that on the 2nd of October of 2001, it was still the position of the Human Rights Watch that the authorities still had not initiated an effective and credible investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no indication at all that such an investigation was underway, and the focus should be on effective and credible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You also recall telling the Prosecution that you would receive -- or that you were provided with reports of the press in Macedonia in relation to your work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in Macedonia, that's correct. After I went to Pakistan and Afghanistan, that became more intermittent.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, that one of your findings was that -- or one of the statements which you've made, in any case, to the Prosecution was that, in fact, Mr. Boskoski had openly tolerated police abuses and that he had personally refused to investigate such abuses? Do you recall making that assertion, Mr. Bouckaert?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: People were beaten to death in the streets of Skopje by police officers in front of large crowds. I certainly think that qualifies as openly tolerating police abuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And concerning your call for a transparent or, I'll use your expression, effective and credible investigation of the August 2001 events in the Ljuboten village, were you aware at the time that on the 12th of August of 2001, an investigation team had been formed with the purpose of entering the village of Ljuboten to investigate? Is that information which you have in your possession?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have information that an investigative judge -- that there had been discussion about bringing an investigative judge to Ljuboten, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that on the 14th of August of 2001, there were at least two unsuccessful attempts by an investigation team composed of an investigative judge, a prosecutor, a forensic expert and a team of the Ministry of the Interior, to enter the village of Ljuboten? Is that information that you had in your possession at the time in August, September, October of 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have such specific information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware that on the 29th of August of 2001, a meeting took place between the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal and the state prosecutor of Macedonia in relation to the situation in Macedonia; is that information that you had in your possession at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 29th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware that during the period, the weeks and months that followed the incident in Ljuboten, a number of meetings between the investigative judge, between prosecutors of the State of Macedonia and between forensic experts of the Skopje Institute took place in relation to the events of Ljuboten? Were you aware of that? Were you aware of that at the time in the weeks or months following the incident?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've explained, I was rather preoccupied with the events in Pakistan and Afghanistan at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree perhaps that the letter suggests -- the letter of 2nd of October of 2001 suggests that your colleagues were not aware or did not have such information in their possession; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: My colleagues did not see any evidence -- any public evidence of an effective or credible investigation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of any requests by yourself or by your colleagues to obtain such information during this period to the Court or to the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware that they were in touch with a large number of people, including the OSCE, NATO, the EU, this Tribunal's OTP, the Macedonian-Helsinki Committee, and that we did not receive any information from any of those sources suggesting that an effective and credible investigation was underway.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were not aware, either, at the time that a formal request for an exhumation and an autopsy had been made by the Prosecutor in relation to the events at Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Can it be clarified which Prosecutor counsel is speaking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking of the state -- or a prosecutor in Macedonia, a public prosecutor in Macedonia. In Skopje, more precisely.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware of efforts being made by the police in Macedonia to obtain information from the villagers in Ljuboten, to obtain information in particular about the identity of the deceased? Is that information which you had in your possession at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Concerning your finding that -- I don't want to misquote you -- that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are we moving to a different topic?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour, it would be a good time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. It's time, I think, Mr. Mettraux, for me to ask about your progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think I have a good and a bad news. The bad news is the usual one, namely, that it will be difficult and, I believe, impossible for me to finish tonight. I, in fact, have two good news. The first good news is we have discussed the matter with the Defence of Mr. Tarculovski, and they have very kindly agreed with the proposal that should the Defence of Mr. Boskoski cover two particular issues, their cross-examination would be extremely limited or nonexistent. And the second good news is if the Trial Chamber is minded to allow the Defence to do that, we would be finished within the first session of tomorrow morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And if that occurred, Mr. Apostolski, what time would you anticipate taking?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that my colleague will encompass the topics which I foresaw. Therefore, I presume that after the cross-examination of my colleagues, I will not be asking questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for your indication, Mr. Apostolski, and the cooperation between both Defence teams. We certainly have some electrical interference. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution believes it needs -- it would need at least one hour for redirect examination tomorrow, and perhaps a bit -- a bit more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, as far as the Chamber can anticipate and control things, I would say that you could anticipate being free at this hour tomorrow. I don't know whether that will help you with your plans, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sure my patience has been tested less than yours, but I talked to the Victims Section and they said that if I can be on the road from here by 6.00, that I will catch my plane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, to facilitate that, could I let Mr. Mettraux have the Chamber's view that at the very most, you should have one hour tomorrow morning, not a full session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will go through the rest of the questions, Your Honour, tonight and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. We adjourn now and resume at 10 minutes past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just before Mr. Mettraux continues, could I mention, an issue has been specifically put to me, whether we are sitting on Monday next week, bearing in mind that we are not sitting Tuesday and Wednesday. A number of the support staff are affected, and I must ask you, Mr. Saxon. You've primarily got the flow of witnesses at the moment, and how it would affect you with a witness to be sure of finishing on Monday of next week, because we then have a two-day break to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution had originally intended to have a witness here specifically for the Monday session. However, the Prosecution decided earlier today to postpone the arrival of that witness for the following reason: Given the length of time that Mr. Bouckaert is taking, and we have another witness waiting here who will probably also take some time, the Prosecution thought the appropriate course of action was not to plan on using any more time on Monday, that it would only use the time required if the following witness carries over beyond Friday, because we had anticipated, Your Honour, in our last witness schedule that we provided to the parties that the following witness would take two full days. Since we were informed last night that the following witness would not start until late Thursday, we anticipate now the following witness will go into Monday. Of course, that remains to be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your anticipation -- it seems -- microphone that's causing the problem. The anticipation is that we will be sitting on Monday, but with the witness that you have --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please turn on mic for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I concluded that observation about we will be sitting on Monday, but dealing with the witness that had been listed for the 4th and the 5th of July, which is Witness M-043. Well, given the time estimations, I think there would be slim chance of that witness finishing on Friday, so we will plan to sit on Monday. I think the listing is to commence sitting at 9.00 in the morning. Very well, thank you for that. Sorry to have delayed you, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll feel entitled to ask for five more minutes tomorrow morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: One hour and five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, were you aware that on the 13th of August of 2001, there was a press conference between -- or, well, I'll call it a press conference, at least a media gathering, after Mr. Boskoski had met with Ambassador Ungaro of the OSCE; can you recall that event on the 13th of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's reflected in our report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall that at the time, the ambassador, Ambassador Ungaro, had asked that an investigation into those events should take place; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware that on the same day, the 13th of August of 2001, a commission was established to look into the circumstances of the events of Ljuboten; are you aware or were you aware of that fact at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is P73, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware that on the 5th of September of 2001, the same day as the day when you issued your report, the commission which had been set up by Mr. Boskoski issued a report about the event in Ljuboten; is that a fact that was within your knowledge at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were not aware that the recommendation of the commission at the time was to carry out an exhumation in Ljuboten and an autopsy of the dead bodies; is that correct? You did not have that information?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this, for the record, Rule 65 ter 239, a Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that on the 7th of September of 2001, the head or president of the commission set up by Mr. Boskoski had issued what is interpreted as either a motion or as in recommendation for exhumation and that this motion was sent to the public prosecutor office in Skopje and to the duty investigative judge in Skopje; are you aware of that document?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were you aware of that document at the time? I'm sorry, I should have asked you that first. Were you aware of that document at that time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you are not aware of the fact that the director of that commission, Mr. Mitrovski, asked for exhumation and autopsy in Ljuboten with the aim of identifying the five corpses and establish the cause of death of the five individuals from the village of Ljuboten; you did not have that information in your possession at the time, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you know at the time or did you have in your possession information suggesting that Mr. Boskoski had personally supported the request or the recommendation made by the commission for an exhumation or an autopsy?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is would be 1D33, 1D34, both of them exhibits, and Rule 65 ter 130 shown to Mr. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact at the time that the request or recommendation which was made by the head of the commission for an autopsy and an exhumation in Ljuboten was taken on by the public prosecutor office in Skopje; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is P55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Bouckaert, that in the month -- in the early month of the year of 2002, Mr. Boskoski offered to assist with the investigation or with the exhumation, rather, in Ljuboten and that his offer of assistance was turned down? Are you aware of that offer on the part of Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the only event I'm aware of in January of 2002 is threats made by Mr. Boskoski against the head of the Macedonian-Helsinki Committee, calling her State Enemy number 1, but I'm not aware of any steps taken towards the investigation or the exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'm very grateful for that. Are you aware of a meeting on the 30th of January of 2002, between inter alia the EUMM, the NATO representative, OSCE representative, ICTY representative, the public prosecutor of the State of Macedonia, to discuss the events of Ljuboten; is that information you have in your possession?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Bouckaert, that your organisation also pressed for a separate investigation by the ICTY into the events of Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We kept the ICTY -- we informed the ICTY of our findings, and as is the general practice of the ICTY, the Office of the Prosecutor, in the absence of a credible investigation, they would then carry out their own investigation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. But the question is: Is that correct that you actually pressed for a separate investigation by the OTP of this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We kept the OTP informed of all of our statements and letters to the government, and they were c.c.'ed on all of this traffic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is identified as Exhibit P353, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, this is again the letter which has been shown to you by the Prosecution in relation to the event of Ljuboten, and I'll ask the Registry to focus on the last paragraph but one on this page, which starts with the words: "Human Rights Watch called ...," and so on. If you can look at this paragraph, Mr. Bouckaert, I'd like to read the last or the second sentence of that paragraph. It reads as follows: "Human Rights Watch pressed for a separate investigation by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia which has jurisdiction over war crimes committed in the Macedonia conflict." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's what you did, you pressed for a separate investigation by the ICTY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And to that effect, is that correct also that you sent a letter to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 5th of September, attached to which was your report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- there was no letter. There was just a short --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: A cover letter?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: A cover letter, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the report was sent to Mr. Morten Bergsmo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Morten Bergsmo, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall who had suggested that you send this report to Mr. Bergsmo at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a call from somebody in the Tribunal on September 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you remember who that person is?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct to understand that your report was prepared, at least in part, with a view to possible prosecution before the ICTY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be correct for all of the reports we do on the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report, you also make an additional finding regarding Mr. -- or two findings, rather. The first finding which you make is that crimes which you believe to be -- or which you recorded in your report were committed by persons whom you say were members of the police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also said that the individuals who had committed the crimes were under the authority of Mr. Boskoski at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you said specifically that they had been under his authority and also under his command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I check the exact language?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly. The first reference is P356, if it could be shown to the witness, please. It's again, Mr. Bouckaert, the record of an interview with Ian Fisher of the "New York Times," and it's the second page of that document. It's 1D00-3576. It's P356. And if we could go to the second page, please. And if we could enlarge the first paragraph on the top left of that document. You are recorded as saying the following, Mr. Bouckaert. It's the last sentence of the first paragraph: "It was done by troops under his authority in an action which he was intimately involved." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was confused about your language about "also under his command."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, isn't that correct, that Human Rights Watch also said that the troops which allegedly committed the crimes were under his command?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can refresh my memory with such a reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, can't you recall or are you saying that it didn't happen?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Neither of those things, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the witness can be --.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He is saying, "Please refresh my memory."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the witness can please be shown document Rule 65 ter 1D344, and the ERN is 1D00-3263.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is the same document that I have shown you before. It's the letter which you sent to Madam Carla Del Ponte and contained within that letter is a letter which you had sent on the 5th of September of 2001 to President Trajkovski. And if we can turn to the third page. It's again the second page where it's said: "We are troubled by the reports that Minister of Interior Ljube Boskoski was in Ljuboten on the 12th of August, the day that the worst abuses were committed. We respectfully request that your government commence a prompt investigation into his role and the conduct of Macedonian troop under his command." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, the word "authority" would have been a better choice of words, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And by that, do I understand, then, your position to be that -- your suggestion, if I may call it that, that the troops which you believe to have committed the crime were under his authority was based solely on the fact that you believe them to have been police officers and him to have been the Minister of Interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think our report is perfectly clear on this point. Mr. Boskoski was present in the village on the day of the worst abuses which were committed by troops under his authority, and that his role in those abuses should be investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, my question is simply this: Your suggestion, and you said you prefer the word "under his authority" to "under his command," was that -- what I'm trying to find out is what you meant by "this." Was it simply the fact, as you said, that, (a), he was in the village and, (b), that he was the Minister of Interior at the time, or was there more to it, to your claim?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As our research has indicated, there was a widespread pattern of police abuse in Macedonia at the time. As I've told this Court, people were beaten to death in the streets of Skopje over a long period of time. There was widespread police abuse at the police stations in Tetovo, Skopje, Kumanovo, Bitola. I think our assessment of Mr. Boskoski's role of the events in Ljuboten should be investigated is related to the whole body of our research. It's not just events in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if I understand your answer properly, and correct me if I'm wrong, you had no indication, other than the fact that Mr. Boskoski was in Ljuboten at the time and that he was the Minister of Interior at the time, to suggest that the troops had been under his authority; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is the Minister of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that correct that because of your experience in the Balkans, you were alert or awake to the possibility of some discrepancies between what I would say is the de jure situation and the de facto situation as far as command or authority is concerned; is that a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Formal command structures were not always reflected on the ground, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at the time of your investigation, did you make any effort to contact anyone within the Ministry of the Interior to investigate the suggestion that the troops had indeed been under the authority of Mr. Boskoski at that time; had you made such a call or a request?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Boskoski is the Minister of Interior. All of the troops are under the authority -- all of the police forces are under the authority of the Minister of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: My question was slightly different, Mr. Bouckaert. I was asking whether you, personally, or whether any member of your organisation made such a request or demand to the Ministry of the Interior for information in relation to this matter.

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you query this matter with any other entity, any other government body in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you query this matter with the President's office in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is now Prosecution Exhibit P303.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, I'll go through this document with you. If you can focus first on the top left-hand corner of this document, you will see it's a document from the Republic of Macedonia, it comes from the Ministry of Defence that's the army -- General Staff Army of the Republic of Macedonia, General Staff. It's dated the 12th of August, 2001, and it comes from the First Guardist Brigade Captain First Class Ljupco Kostadinov. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just the subject of the note is: "Report on actions and situation in 3rd Guardist Brigade, village of Ljuboten"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like you to focus on the first paragraph of that document, which starts with the words: "On 10 August 2001. At 2130 hours, a group of around 40 persons came to the school in the village of Ljubanci. The ground was headed by the person Johan Tarculovski, Head of the Agency, Kometa," that's what the document says, "who come from the village Ljubanci. After some time more persons arrived, whereby the number increased to around 60, 70 persons. The MVR truck arrived from which weapons, ammunition, bombs, and bazookas were distributed. The persons were wearing MVR uniforms. These persons asked Major Mitre Despodov, who is commander of the 3rd Guardist Brigade, to provide them with a place to sleep in the mountain lodge in village Ljubanci. Major Despodov asked them on whose orders they had come, they said that this is known to the President and no one else should about their stay. Major Despodov asked them what their role is here, they answered that they have the task to enter the village Ljuboten and to conduct a search and cleaning of the terrain." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please. And I will ask you to focus your attention on the second or third paragraph starting with the words: "On Saturday, 11 August 2001 ..." And it reads as follows: "On Saturday, 11 August 2001, the above-listed persons, headed by Johan Tarculovski, conducted reconnaissance in the village Ljuboten and in the village they shot at dogs that barked at them. At around 1700 to 1730 the person Johan Tarculovski asked Major Mitre Despodov to shoot at targets in the village Ljuboten which they previously had determined precisely together decided with Major Mitre Despodov. Major Despodov did not want to open fire upon the above-mentioned targets without orders, requested approval from his superior. Around 1800 to 1900 hours, first the person, Johan, talked to the president of the state and then Major Despodov personally talked with the President. The President asked him whether he's under the command of General Sokol. Major Despodov answered, 'Yes.' The President told him, 'Good, I will talk to General Sokol, and I will call you again.'". Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there is simply another paragraph which I would like to draw your attention to. It's two paragraphs down starting with the words: "The reservists ..." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says: "The reservists, wearing MVR uniforms, advanced in the village up to arriving at the bridge, where there was a check-point and the house of person Kenan." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's consistent, isn't it, with the report that -- or with the letter that I read to you earlier from Mr. Kostadinov?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'mm-hmm.
