utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like the witness now to be shown what is Prosecution Exhibit P304.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, this is -- this will be again another military report, dated also the 12th of August of 2001, and it's a Prosecution exhibit. If you can focus again on the top left corner, you will see it comes from the Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Defence, General Staff, and this is the 1st Guardist Brigade. And it is dated the 12th of August of 2001. It's a report about the situation in the area of 3rd Guardist Brigade Battalion in the village Ljuboten. And again if you look at the first paragraph, it records the fact that a group of about 40 persons arrived to the house of the owner," and it repeats the same thing of Kometa security company, Johan Tarculovski, "in Ljubanci on 10 August 2001 at 2130." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if you go to the second paragraph, it says the following: "The action about which none was supposed to know on the order of the President was supposed to begin on 11 August 2001 at 4.30." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if you go to the last paragraph on that page, there is a statement to the following effect: "Between 1800 and 1900 on 11 August 2001, Johan Tarculovski personally called the President from the command post of the 3rd Battalion of the 1st Guardist Brigade, and after a brief discussion the President requested that Major Mitre Despodov speak to him in person." And there's a parenthesis: "As the commander showed up, the President asked him, 'If you are under the command of General Sokol,' and latter said, 'Yes.' And the President told him, 'Good, I will speak to General Sokol will call you back." So just at this stage you would agree that this is consistent with the previous one, is that correct, the other military report that showed you a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn to the third and last page of that document, please. I will ask you to look at the last paragraph, first, as you will see, it's signed by Mr. Kopacev, commander, and the last paragraph says this: "Finally, I would like to mention that the commander of the 3rd/1 Brigade knew about the action on 10th August 2001 and together with Johan Tarculovski were planning the action, but they did not inform anybody. For that, he received guarantee from Johan Tarculovski that he would not bear any responsibility for the action, and he would be protected personally by the President." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like now to draw your attention to the evidence of Mr. Despodov which is referred to on a number of occasions in this report. Your Honour, this is the transcript of the 25th of June, 2007, with Major Despodov, and it is at page 2580-2581. Mr. Despodov was shown one of the reports by the Prosecution, and he was asked about one of the reports, and which states as follows. I will read the question from the Prosecution to you. It says -- the top paragraph on this, actually, it is the second paragraph. It starts with: "On Saturday, 11 August 2001, the above-listed persons, headed by Johan Tarculovski, conducted reconnaissance in the village of Ljuboten, and in the village they shot at dogs that barked at them. At around 1730 hours, the person Johan Tarculovski asked Major Mitre Despodov to shoot at targets in the village of Ljuboten which they previously had determined precisely together with Major Mitre Despodov. Major Despodov did not want to open fire upon the above-mentioned targets without orders, requested approval from the superior. Around 1800 to 1900 hours, first the person, Johan, talked to the president of the state, and then Major Despodov personally talked with the President. The President asked him whether he is under the command of General Sokol. Major Despodov answered, 'Yes.' The President told him, 'Good, I will talk to General Sokol and then I will talk to you again.'" And then the witness was asked by the Prosecutor: "Do you recall that event happening?" And the witness said: "I remember, and I confirm that this conversation that is mentioned here with the President as it is stated is correct, and the rest of it, no." And then he is asked: "Did you ever receive a call from the President after this conversation you reference in this paragraph?" And he says: "I already mentioned during this meeting -- during the meeting, while it lasted on Friday with the people that I already mentioned, Mr. Johan talked to the President, and during the moment while he was talking, he handed the phone to me and said, 'Mr. Despodov, somebody wants to talk to you. The President wants to talk to you.' I cannot really recall the wording. However, this was the essence. When I took over the phone, by the voice on the other side of the line, I could recognise the voice of the President. And not to repeat myself, he said what was already mentioned, whether I was really indeed the commander, whether I was Mitre Despodov, the commander of the battalion, whether I recognised the voice, whether I'm sure who the person was, et cetera. I had to say that I had met the President on several occasions before that. I was talking to him on the phone because, beside my regular tasks and obligation in the brigade during the official welcoming parties and sending off of the President, I had the task of being the cameraman and to document these kind of events at the airport before the Parliament building," et cetera. Would you agree that again this evidence, sir, is consistent with the two documents, the two military reports that I have shown to you?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the sections I've seen of those reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. There is another document which I would like to show to Mr. Bouckaert --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could the documents that have been marked for identification, P303 and P304, now be admitted, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They presently are marked. In your re-examination, you may move that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply for the record, Your Honour, the reason why, I believe, we hadn't admitted them at the time was because Mr. Kostadinov is scheduled to appear as a witness, and I believe that this was the reason why it was identified in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Are you happy to move for their admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We would have no objection. We had understood that at the time the position was that it would be better to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm being very technical at this hour of day. It's your cross-examination, so I would like to have the Prosecutor moving and an exhibit to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We would have no objection to the admission, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, I would like to show you another document at this stage, which is Rule 65 ter 760, and it has an ERN number of N001-4885. And the Macedonian version of that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, I see that my answer was recorded incorrectly.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters would like to point that we are lagging way behind, so if you could wait a while until we catch up with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, could you indicate the line at which you have identified an error in the record, please?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is line 2. My answer says: "With the exception of those sections you've read to me" and it should say -- sorry, it's no longer on my screen. It should say it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll put the question again to you because it's disappearing from the screen. The question was: Would you agree that this is the same as the military report as I had shown to you, is that correct, that the evidence of Mr. Despodov is consistent with those parts of the report which I have read to you, the reports?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's consistent with the sections you have read to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And if the witness could be shown Rule 65 ter 670, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, this is another statement taken by the Office of the Prosecution of Mr. Zlatko Keskovski, and the statement was taken on 7th of February of 2005. Mr. Keskovski was a member of the security arrangements of the President of Macedonia, Mr. Trajkovski, at the time. If we can turn to page 9 of this document, please. If we can focus in particular on paragraph 39 first. Mr. Keskovski is recorded as having said the following to the Prosecution: "After the above-mentioned conversation, Johan Tarculovski called on my mobile phone. He said that in Ljuboten there is an action being prepared. I asked him what it means. He replied that in Ljuboten, there are fortifications of terrorists -- of the terrorists. He allegedly received this information from the Ljubanci villagers. They also told him that the people responsible for the death of the soldiers at Ljubotenski Bacila were still in the village Ljuboten. I asked him who was preparing the action, and he replied that it was the police and the army units. I asked him what the problem was. He said that the problem was a certain army major, I do not know his name, who did not want to undertake any activities because he did not receive any orders from his superior officer. The major was allegedly commanding a mortar ARM unit which, according to Tarculovski, was supposed to participate in the organised action. I understood from Johan Tarculovski that the infantry could not enter the village unless they had support from the artillery. As I spoke to Tarculovski, I understood he was in Ljubanci village at the moment along with the major of the army." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then at paragraph 40 it says this: "I told Tarculovski to put the major on the phone. I did not ask the major about his name, only his rank and superior officer. Therefore, I did not know his name. The person told me that he was in rank of major and his superior was General Sokol Mitrovski, who the President's adjutant. He said that he did not receive any order for firing the mortars and that he will do so only if he receives an order." And it continues: "I still held on the phone, and I explained the President what the situation was. The President asked me to give him the phone because he wanted to talk to the major. Before handing the phone to the President, I asked the Major if he would obey an order coming directly from the Supreme Commander; that is, the President. The Major replied that the President was the supreme superior, and he would have to obey the order from the President. In that period of time, the President was under pressure from the public because he was thought to have failed to use the army appropriately in dealing with terrorists. Therefore, he wanted to speak to the Major." And if we can turn to the next page, at paragraph 41 Mr. Keskovski is recorded as saying the following: "The President asked what his rank and superior's name. I did not hear any replies from the Major to the President, but I heard as the President told the Major to make sure that the operation goes according to the plan, and he would call his superior, General Sokol Mitrovski. There were not any other contacts that I know of from Johan Tarculovski on that day to me. We did not discuss the issue with the President later that day because it was considered regular activity in that period of time." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I'm not sure what the relevance of all this information is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that consistent again with the military documents or the passages of the military documents which I have shown to you earlier?

utterances.speaker: PETER BOUCKAERT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness now be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D444, and it has an ERN 1D00-4086.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bouckaert, this is a letter which was sent to us by the Prosecution pursuant to Rule 68. This is exculpatory material, and it is sent by senior trial attorney, Mr. Saxon. Well, it appears that the documents may not be uploaded, Your Honour. It seems to be now. I'll read the text to you, Mr. Bouckaert. This is a letter, as I mentioned, from Mr. Saxon dated the 1st of September of 2006. This is addressed to Ms. Residovic, Mr. Gorgo [phoen], and Mr. Apostolski. The subject of the letter is disclosure of Pec [phoen] 29 potentially exculpatory information under Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm very grateful. If we could focus on the lower part of the document, or the middle part, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You can see Mr. Saxon addressed the letter to us in the following term: "As part of the Prosecution's continuing obligation, it hereby provides to you the following information that it believes could be potentially exculpatory to the case of one or more accused," and then the section which is provided for us --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry to interrupt. I did not anticipate, when I sent this letter nearly a year ago, that it would be used in public session. I believe we are, and I was wondering whether we could simply do this in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now for the day, to resume tomorrow at 2.15.
